questiontext.text: Match the compounds given in Column I with the effects given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Halogen-containing organic compounds have diverse physiological, pharmacological, and medical applications.

Step 2: Analysis of Individual Compounds
- Chloramphenicol is a chlorine-containing broad-spectrum antibiotic produced by soil microorganisms, specifically used for the clinical treatment of typhoid fever.
- Thyroxine is an iodine-containing hormone secreted by the thyroid gland; an inadequate level of iodine or thyroxine leads to enlargement of the thyroid gland, known as goiter.
- Chloroquine is a synthetic halogenated quinoline derivative extensively utilized in the prophylaxis and therapy of malaria caused by the plasmodium parasite.
- Chloroform (\(\mathrm{CHCl}_3\)) was historically utilized as an inhalation anaesthetic in surgical procedures.
- Blood substituent is an extra effect, typically associated with fluorine-containing synthetic perfluorocarbons.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Chloramphenicol matches Typhoid fever, Thyroxine matches Goiter, Chloroquine matches Malaria, and Chloroform matches Anaesthetic.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MATCHING_Q80 - Reaction types and classes of halogen compounds

questiontext.text: Match the items of Column I and Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Reactions and chemical classifications of haloalkanes relate to specific mechanistic pathways, rules, and practical applications.

Step 2: Analysis of Individual Items
- \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) reaction proceeds via a planar carbocation intermediate upon which nucleophilic attack occurs from both faces with equal probability, leading to racemisation in optically active substrates.
- Chemicals in fire extinguisher include volatile halogenated hydrocarbons such as chlorobromocarbons (and halons/chlorofluorocarbons) which act by smothering flames and interrupting free-radical combustion chains.
- Bromination of alkenes involves electrophilic addition of molecular bromine across the carbon-carbon double bond, yielding vicinal dibromides (vic-dibromides) with bromine atoms on adjacent carbons.
- Alkylidene halides have two halogen atoms attached to the very same carbon atom, which defines them as geminal dihalides (gem-dihalides).
- Elimination of \(\mathrm{HX}\) from an alkyl halide (dehydrohalogenation) preferentially yields the more highly substituted, more stable alkene in accordance with the Saytzeff rule.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
\(\mathrm{S_N1}\) reaction matches Racemisation, Chemicals in fire extinguisher matches Chlorobromocarbons, Bromination of alkenes matches vic-dibromides, Alkylidene halides matches gem-dihalides, and Elimination of \(\mathrm{HX}\) from alkylhalide matches Saytzeff rule.

questiontext.text: Match the structures of compounds given in Column I with the classes of compounds given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Halogen derivatives are classified according to the hybridization and nature of the carbon atom to which the halogen atom is directly attached.

Step 2: Structural Evaluation
- \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH(X)}-\mathrm{CH}_3\): The halogen atom is bonded to a saturated secondary \(\mathrm{sp}^3\)-hybridized carbon atom belonging to an aliphatic alkyl chain; hence, it is an alkyl halide.
- \(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{X}\): The halogen atom is bonded to an \(\mathrm{sp}^3\)-hybridized carbon atom adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond (\(\mathrm{C=C}\)); hence, it is an allyl halide.
- Chlorobenzene (): The halogen atom is bonded directly to an \(\mathrm{sp}^2\)-hybridized aromatic ring carbon; hence, it is an aryl halide.
- \(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{X}\): The halogen atom is bonded directly to an \(\mathrm{sp}^2\)-hybridized vinylic carbon atom of a carbon-carbon double bond; hence, it is a vinyl halide.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
\(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH(X)}-\mathrm{CH}_3\) matches Alkyl halide, \(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{X}\) matches Allyl halide, chlorobenzene matches Aryl halide, and \(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{X}\) matches Vinyl halide.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HALOALKANES_AND_HALOARENES_MATCHING_Q82 - Reaction types of halogenated organic molecules

questiontext.text: Match the reactions given in Column I with the types of reactions given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Reactions involving halo compounds fall into fundamental organic reaction types: electrophilic aromatic substitution, nucleophilic aromatic substitution, electrophilic addition, nucleophilic aliphatic substitution, and base-induced \(\beta\)-elimination.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Reaction
- Reaction (i) (): Chlorobenzene reacts with chlorine in the presence of iron catalyst to form ortho and para dichlorobenzene via generation of a chloronium electrophile; this is an electrophilic aromatic substitution.
- Reaction (ii) (\(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}_2 + \mathrm{HBr} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH(Br)}-\mathrm{CH}_3\)): Hydrogen bromide adds across the double bond of propene following Markovnikov's rule; this is an electrophilic addition.
- Reaction (iii) (): Hydrolysis of a secondary benzylic iodide generates an exceptionally stable resonance-stabilized benzylic carbocation before hydroxide attack; this is a nucleophilic substitution (\(\mathrm{S_N}1\)).
- Reaction (iv) (): 4-Nitrochlorobenzene reacts with aqueous hydroxide ion to replace chlorine by hydroxyl group, promoted by the electron-withdrawing nitro group; this is a nucleophilic aromatic substitution.
- Reaction (v) (): 2-Bromobutane undergoes dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic potassium hydroxide to give but-2-ene as the major product; this is a Saytzeff elimination.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Reaction (i) matches Electrophilic aromatic substitution, Reaction (ii) matches Electrophilic addition, Reaction (iii) matches Nucleophilic substitution (\(\mathrm{S_N}1\)), Reaction (iv) matches Nucleophilic aromatic substitution, and Reaction (v) matches Saytzeff elimination.

Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to IUPAC nomenclature rules for unsaturated halides, the principal functional group is the double bond, which receives the lowest possible locant in the parent chain, followed by substituents (alkyl and halogen) listed alphabetically.

Step 2: Structural Analysis
- Structure (i): The longest chain containing the double bond has five carbon atoms (pent-2-ene). Numbering from the left gives the double bond locant 2 and the bromine substituent at carbon-4; hence, its IUPAC name is 4-bromopent-2-ene.
- Structure (ii): The longest chain has five carbon atoms with a double bond at position 2 (pent-2-ene). Substituents are a methyl group at carbon-3 and a bromine atom at carbon-4; hence, its IUPAC name is 4-bromo-3-methylpent-2-ene.
- Structure (iii): The longest chain has four carbon atoms with a double bond at position 2 (but-2-ene). Numbering gives bromine at carbon-1 and a methyl group at carbon-2; hence, its IUPAC name is 1-bromo-2-methylbut-2-ene.
- Structure (iv): The longest chain has five carbon atoms with a double bond at position 2 (pent-2-ene). A methyl group is at carbon-2 and a bromine atom is at carbon-1; hence, its IUPAC name is 1-bromo-2-methylpent-2-ene.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Structure (i) matches 4-Bromopent-2-ene, Structure (ii) matches 4-Bromo-3-methylpent-2-ene, Structure (iii) matches 1-Bromo-2-methylbut-2-ene, and Structure (iv) matches 1-Bromo-2-methylpent-2-ene.

questiontext.text: Match the reactions given in Column I with the names given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Named chemical reactions in organic chemistry describe classical synthetic methodologies with well-defined reagents and substrates.

Step 2: Identification of Named Reactions
- Reaction (i) (): An aryl halide reacts with an alkyl halide in the presence of sodium metal in dry ether to yield an alkylarene; this is the Wurtz Fittig reaction.
- Reaction (ii) (): Two molecules of an aryl halide couple together in the presence of sodium metal in dry ether to form a biaryl (diphenyl); this is the Fittig reaction.
- Reaction (iii) (): Treatment of a diazonium salt with cuprous halide (\(\mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{X}_2\)) results in replacement of the diazonium group by halogen to form a haloarene; this is the Sandmeyer reaction.
- Reaction (iv) (\(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{Cl} + \mathrm{NaI} \xrightarrow{\text{dry acetone}} \mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{I} + \mathrm{NaCl}\)): Reaction of an alkyl chloride with sodium iodide in dry acetone to prepare an alkyl iodide via precipitation of sodium chloride is the Finkelstein reaction.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Reaction (i) matches Wurtz Fittig reaction, Reaction (ii) matches Fittig reaction, Reaction (iii) matches Sandmeyer reaction, and Reaction (iv) matches Finkelstein reaction.
